nodes.summary: Every component Bayes factor is positive.
nodes.title: Positivity of component Bayes factors

nodes.summary: The Bayes factor of component `i` at the observed value: the ratio of its score function under selection to its score function under neutrality.
nodes.title: Bayes factor of a component statistic

nodes.summary: The CMS score is the ratio of the two joint densities.
nodes.title: CMS score as a ratio of joint densities

nodes.summary: The CMS score: the product of the component Bayes factors.
nodes.title: Composite of multiple signals (CMS) score

nodes.summary: A composite-score model (Grossman et al. 2010): a prior probability `prior` that the site is under selection, and for each of the `k` component statistics a positive score function `sel` under selection and `neut` under neutrality (unnormalized densities: only positivity is assumed). Conditionally on the hypothesis the components are independent, which is what makes the joint scores the products below. The…
nodes.title: Composite selection score model

nodes.summary: No lineage escapes at the swept site itself, and nowhere else.
nodes.title: Escape probability vanishes only at the swept site

nodes.summary: The escape-probability profile determines the sweep location and its strength. Positivity of one of the two strength parameters is enough: the location is the unique zero of that profile, and the strengths then agree by injectivity of `exp`.
nodes.title: Escape profile determines sweep location and strength

nodes.summary: The probability that a lineage at position `y` escapes a sweep located at `x`, with compound strength parameter `α > 0`: `1 - exp (-α |y - x|)` (Kim and Stephan 2002; Nielsen et al. 2005). The parameter `α` is proportional to the recombination rate per unit distance divided by the selection coefficient.
nodes.title: Probability of escaping a selective sweep

nodes.summary: On the log scale the evidence is additive: the log posterior odds are the log prior odds plus the sum of the log Bayes factors of the component statistics.
nodes.title: Additivity of evidence on the log-odds scale

nodes.summary: A mixture of two distinct laws determines its mixing weight.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the mixing weight of a two-component mixture

nodes.summary: The posterior probability is a strictly increasing function of the CMS score, so the two rankings of sites agree.
nodes.title: Posterior probability is strictly increasing in the CMS score

nodes.summary: Bayes-rule identity for conditionally independent components: the posterior odds of selection are the prior odds times the CMS score. This is an algebraic identity for the normalized score; it is a genuine Bayes rule only under the normalization hypothesis of `sum_joint_eq_one`.
nodes.title: Posterior odds equal prior odds times the CMS score

nodes.summary: The normalized composite score: the normalized ratio of the products of the component score functions. This is the posterior probability of selection given the observed component values when the score functions are normalized densities (see `sum_joint_eq_one` for the normalization hypothesis).
nodes.title: Normalized composite score

nodes.summary: The model is a probability model: with normalised component score functions (each a density with respect to a common base measure), the joint distribution of the observations sums to one. This is the validity hypothesis that makes `posterior` a genuine Bayes posterior.
nodes.title: Normalization of the composite score model

nodes.summary: Identifiability of the sweep parameters from the per-site frequency spectra. If the neutral spectrum `f` and the post-sweep spectrum `g` differ, and two sweep parameter pairs give the same mixture at every position, then the parameters coincide. This is what the composite likelihood of SweepFinder maximises over.
nodes.title: Identifiability of sweep parameters from frequency spectra

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
